questions.question:
Choose the correct option to specify the meaning of the highlighted idiom.

"I know you are ready. **Go break a leg now**."

options.text: Ask someone not to go for a task

questions.solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Say Good Luck to someone**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Break a leg"** is commonly used to wish someone good luck before they perform or attempt something. (शुभकामनाएं देना) • **Example:** Before her big performance, her friends said, "Break a leg!" to encourage her. • The highlighted idiom does not literally mean to break a leg but is instead a way of expressing encouragement and well-wishing. (हिंदी में: शुभकामनाएं देने के लिए इस्तेमाल किया जाता है) • **Example:** "Break a leg! You'll do great in your interview." Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Say Good Luck to someone**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: Ask someone not to go for a task** (किसी को काम करने से मना करना) • **Example:** This option is incorrect as "Break a leg" does not mean to discourage or stop someone. • **Option 3: Say Bad Luck to someone** (किसी को दुर्भाग्य की कामना करना) • **Example:** This option is incorrect because the idiom "Break a leg" conveys good luck, not bad luck. • **Option 4: Not saying anything to someone** (किसी से कुछ भी न कहना) • **Example:** This option is incorrect because "Break a leg" is a phrase actively used to wish someone good luck. 34:Te81, The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Take risks.

questions.question:
Identify the meaning of the phrase highlighted in bold.

Looking at the situation, the best plan of action would be to **throw caution to the wind**.

options.text: Take a meeting and ask for everyone's input

questions.solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Take risks. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The phrase **"throw caution to the wind"** means: • To act in a reckless manner, without worrying about the risks or possible negative outcomes. (बिना किसी चिंता के जोखिम लेना या संभावित नकारात्मक परिणामों के बारे में अन्यथा सोचना) • **Example:** She decided to throw caution to the wind and invested all her savings in the new startup. • **"Correct answer"** means: • Referring to the specific answer that properly defines or fits the context of the question. (सही उत्तर) • **Example:** The correct answer to the quiz question assured him a perfect score. Therefore, the phrase "throw caution to the wind" in the given context means: **Take risks**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Ignore the situation** (स्थिति को नजरअंदाज करना): To deliberately avoid dealing with or paying attention to a particular situation. • **Example:** It is not advisable to ignore the situation when serious problems arise. • **Playing safe** (सुरक्षित खेलना): To act in a cautious and risk-averse manner to avoid potential problems or dangers. • **Example:** In uncertain times, it is often better to play safe with your investments. • **Take a meeting and ask for everyone's input** (एक बैठक करना और सभी से राय पूछना): To hold a discussion involving all relevant parties to gather opinions or suggestions. • **Example:** Before making a final decision, the manager decided to take a meeting and ask for everyone's input. 35:Tadf, **The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence.

options.text: Mitali's hair is long and black.
Either of the alternatives seem to present major difficulties
One of the cars in the garage is fifty years old.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To answer this question, let's break down each sentence to identify the grammatically correct and incorrect ones:**

__
 
• **A. Mitali's hair is long and black.**

 
 
• When referring to all the hair on a person's head, "hair" is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **B. Either of the alternatives seem to present major difficulties.**
 __
 
• The word "Either" is a distributive pronoun that always acts as a singular subject. Therefore, it requires a singular verb ("seems").
 
• The sentence is erroneous__ because "seem" is the plural form of the verb.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "Either of the alternatives **seems** to present major difficulties."
 
 
 
• **C. One of the cars in the garage is fifty years old.**
 __
 
• In the phrase "One of the [plural noun]," the subject is "One," which is singular. The verb "is" correctly agrees with "One."
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **D. Sharon has six brothers.**
 __
 
• The singular subject "Sharon" is correctly paired with the singular verb "has."
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• __So, out of the given options, sentence 2 is the only grammatically incorrect sentence__.
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2."**

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:**

The detective inquired ______ the suspect's whereabouts during the investigation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**about**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The preposition "**about**" is used when inquiring or asking for information related to a topic, subject, or situation.
 
• In the given sentence, the detective is asking for information regarding the suspect's whereabouts during the investigation, which makes "**about**" the most appropriate choice.
 
• **Option 1 (of)** is incorrect as it implies possession or association, which is not suitable here.
 
• **Option 2 (for)** is incorrect as it is typically used to indicate purpose or intention, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 4 (to)** is incorrect as it is used to indicate direction or movement, which is irrelevant in this sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The detective inquired **about**__ the suspect's whereabouts during the investigation."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "of"** is incorrect as it implies belonging or connection, not inquiry.
 
• **Option 2: "for"** is incorrect because it implies seeking something for a purpose, which does not match the context of asking for information.
 
• **Option 4: "to"** is incorrect as it implies direction, movement, or relation, which does not apply here.
</ul

questions.question:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:

He offered a great __**deal**__ on the used car.

options.text: The two countries signed a new trade deal.
The magician will deal out the cards for the trick.
I found a great deal on airline tickets.
The business deal was finalized this morning.

questions.solution:

• The word **"deal"** has multiple meanings, making it a homonym. In English, "deal" can mean an agreement or transaction, or the act of distributing something. (समझौता या बांटना) 
 
 
• **Example 1: Transaction:** He offered a great deal on the used car. (The word "deal" here refers to a transaction or bargain.) 
 
• **Example 2: Distribution:** The magician will deal out the cards for the trick. (The word "deal" here refers to the act of distributing or handing out cards.) 
 
 
• In Option 2, "deal" refers to the act of distributing cards, which is a homonym of the highlighted usage in the question. 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. "The magician will deal out the cards for the trick."**

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The evidence could not have been overlooked by an experienced detective, a fact that was later emphasized.

options.text: An experienced detective could not have overlooked the evidence, a fact that was later emphasized
The evidence could not overlook an experienced detective.
An experienced detective could not overlook the evidence.
The evidence was not overlooked by an experienced detective, a fact that was later emphasized.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 

• Active voice structure: The subject performs the action directly on the object. 

• In the passive voice, the sentence was: "The evidence could not have been overlooked by an experienced detective, a fact that was later emphasized." 

• To convert to active voice: Place the original subject "an experienced detective" at the beginning. 

• Change the passive verb phrase "could not have been overlooked" to "could not have overlooked" (active voice structure). 

• Ensure the rest of the sentence remains intact, including "a fact that was later emphasized" for clarity. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"An experienced detective could not have overlooked the evidence, a fact that was later emphasized."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 

• **Option 2: **"The evidence could not overlook an experienced detective." – Incorrect because the object "evidence" cannot perform the action. 

• **Option 3: **"An experienced detective could not overlook the evidence." – Incorrect because it omits "a fact that was later emphasized," changing the meaning. 

• **Option 4: **"The evidence was not overlooked by an experienced detective, a fact that was later emphasized." – This is the original passive voice sentence, not active voice. 
</ul

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The suspect was believed to have been seen near the crime scene.

options.text: Someone believed that the suspect was seen near the crime scene.
They believed someone had seen the suspect near the crime scene.
The suspect was seen near the crime scene, it was believed.
People believed that someone had seen the suspect near the crime scene.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice.
 
• To convert it into the active voice, the subject performing the action must be identified and placed at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• In this case, the subject performing the action is "someone" or "they," as implied by the context.
 
• The active form of the sentence should follow the structure: "[Subject] + [verb] + [object]."
 
• The correct active voice structure for this sentence is: "They believed someone had seen the suspect near the crime scene."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"They believed someone had seen the suspect near the crime scene."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Someone believed that the suspect was seen near the crime scene." – Although plausible, it alters the original meaning slightly by emphasizing "someone."
 
• **Option 3:** "The suspect was seen near the crime scene, it was believed." – This is still in passive voice and does not follow the active voice structure.
 
• **Option 4:** "People believed that someone had seen the suspect near the crime scene." – This introduces "people," which changes the subject unnecessarily.

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that he would be travelling the following month.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"I will be travelling" becomes "he would be travelling"**
 
 
• The pronoun "I" is changed to "he" to match the subject in the indirect speech.
 
• The modal verb "will" is changed to "would" to reflect the past tense reporting.
 
 
 
• **"next month" becomes "the following month"**
 
 
• Time expressions are changed in indirect speech to reflect their relative context.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The sentence is restructured to maintain the meaning and grammatical accuracy.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said that he would be travelling the following month."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said that he will be travelling the next month." 
 
 
• Incorrect: "will" is not changed to "would" as required in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said that he would have been travelling the following month." 
 
 
• Incorrect: "would have been travelling" changes the meaning to a past hypothetical scenario, which does not match the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said that he was travelling next month." 
 
 
• Incorrect: "was travelling" does not match the original future tense of the sentence.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The teacher asked the students if they had finished their homework.

options.text: The teacher said to the students, "Have you finished your homework?"
The teacher said to the students, "Did you finish your homework?"
The teacher said to the students, "Have you finished their homework?"
The teacher said to the students, "Had you finished your homework?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The teacher asked the students if they had finished their homework.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"if they had finished" becomes "Have you finished"**
 
 
• Indirect question "if they had finished" is converted to direct question "Have you finished."
 
• Pronoun "they" is changed to "you" to match direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "asked"
 
• Converted to: "said to," maintaining the context of addressing the students.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "Have" and ends with a question mark "?".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The teacher said to the students, 'Have you finished your homework?'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The teacher said to the students, 'Did you finish your homework?'"
 
 
• Changes the tense from present perfect "Have you finished" to simple past "Did you finish," altering the meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The teacher said to the students, 'Have you finished their homework?'"
 
 
• Pronoun "their" is incorrect, as it does not match the direct speech context.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "The teacher said to the students, 'Had you finished your homework?'"
 
 
• Changes the tense to past perfect "Had you finished," which is inconsistent with the original sentence.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

They must have taken the intricate artifacts from the museum's security vault with great care.

options.text: The intricate artifacts must have been taken with great care from the museum's security vault.
The intricate artifacts had to be taken with great care from the museum's security vault.
It must have been the intricate artifacts that were taken from the museum's security vault with great care.
The intricate artifacts should have been taken from the museum's security vault with great care.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. 
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "They must have taken the intricate artifacts from the museum's security vault with great care." 
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the intricate artifacts" at the beginning. 
 
• Change the active verb form "must have taken" to "must have been taken" (perfect modal passive). 
 
• Retain the prepositional phrase "with great care" and "from the museum's security vault" for clarity. 
 
• Ensure the sentence structure remains logical and grammatically correct in passive voice. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The intricate artifacts must have been taken with great care from the museum's security vault."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 2: **"The intricate artifacts had to be taken with great care from the museum's security vault." – Incorrect as it changes the modal verb "must" to "had to," altering the meaning. 
 
• **Option 3: **"It must have been the intricate artifacts that were taken from the museum's security vault with great care." – Wordy and indirect, not the best passive transformation. 
 
• **Option 4: **"The intricate artifacts should have been taken from the museum's security vault with great care." – Incorrect as it changes the modal verb "must" to "should," altering the meaning.

questions.question: What does the word "Suspect" refer to?

options.text: A person who believes in something without proof
A person who is believed to be involved in a crime
A person who has been wrongly accused

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. A person who is believed to be involved in a crime**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Suspect"** refers to someone who is believed to have committed or participated in a crime or unlawful act. (संदिग्ध व्यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example:** The police questioned the suspect after finding evidence at the crime scene.
 
 
• In legal contexts, a suspect is not proven guilty but is under investigation or suspicion. (संदेह के घेरे में व्यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example:** The suspect denied all allegations made against him.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. A person who is believed to be involved in a crime**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: A person who believes in something without proof** (बिना सबूत के कुछ मानने वाला व्यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example:** A person who believes in conspiracy theories often accepts ideas without proof.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A person who investigates crimes** (अपराधों की जांच करने वाला व्यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example:** The detective worked tirelessly to solve the murder case.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A person who has been wrongly accused** (जिसे गलत तरीके से आरोपी बनाया गया हो)
 
 
• **Example:** The wrongly accused man was later proven innocent in court.
